For the purposes of this document a testing season is the twelve months beginning on 1 October. Every accession is tested once per season, viability is reported as a season average, and the storage review takes the two most recent seasons together. Trays are sown in fives and held at the bench temperature stated on the accession card. Counts are made at seven, fourteen and twenty-one days by the technician on duty. Where germination falls below half the accession's first measured figure, regeneration is scheduled in the following season. Bench notes are kept in the laboratory book and totals transferred to the accession card.

Each line carries the time, then the vehicle count, then foot passengers, then sea state, with the fields separated by a solidus and no spaces, and the date given at the head of the page as day-month-year in figures. Delays of more than ten minutes are noted in the margin with the cause in words. The log is collected on the first of the month by the office launch and a fresh book left in its place. Nothing is erased; corrections are struck through once and initialled.
